fullDescription:
Two days covering the two landscapes people confuse with each other: Ninh Binh and Ha Long Bay.

They are the same geology doing two different things. Ninh Binh is often called the inland Ha Long Bay, and that is accurate: the same limestone karst towers, but rising out of rice paddies and a river instead of the sea. You move through it on a small rowing boat, and the rowers famously work the oars with their feet.

Day one is the inland half. Hoa Lu was Vietnam's capital in the tenth century, under the Dinh and early Le dynasties, before it moved to what is now Hanoi; the temples there sit in a bowl of limestone that made the site defensible. Tam Coc is the boat trip, three caves the river runs through, with the karsts close enough on both sides to touch. Mua Caves is the climb: around 500 stone steps to a dragon statue on the ridge, and the view from the top is the photograph that made Ninh Binh famous.

Day two is Ha Long Bay itself, where the same towers rise out of the sea instead.

The night is spent in a bungalow rather than a hotel block, which in Ninh Binh usually means being out among the karsts rather than in town.

Transport is a 22-seat limousine bus, which on Vietnamese roads means reclining seats and space rather than a coach.

We book with Halong Excursion directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the limousine bus, bottled water, an English-speaking guide throughout, entrance fees, and kayaking or a bamboo boat at Luon Cave.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Ninh Binh and Ha Long: the same karst, inland and at sea
Hoa Lu, Vietnam's capital in the tenth century
Tam Coc by rowing boat, through three river caves
Around 500 steps up Mua Caves for the ridge view
Night in a bungalow among the karsts, not a hotel block

fullDescription:
Ha Long the city rather than Ha Long the bay, which almost every visitor skips entirely.

Nearly everyone who comes here boards a boat and leaves. The city behind the pier is a working provincial capital of a few hundred thousand people, built on coal money, and it has the things a coal-and-sea town has rather than the things a resort has.

Quang Ninh Museum is the reason to do this tour. It is a black glass box on the waterfront designed by the Spanish architect Salvador Perez Arroyo, and it is genuinely one of the better museums in Vietnam: the building reflects the bay in its facade, and inside it runs from the region's marine geology through the coal-mining history that built the city, including a reconstructed mine shaft.

Long Tien Pagoda sits under Bai Tho Mountain and is the largest pagoda in the city, built in the 1940s in the style of Hanoi's older temples.

The seafood market is where the town actually eats. Ha Long's catch comes in fresh and the market is the local price rather than the pier price.

This is the trip for a day when the bay cruises are cancelled for weather, which happens with some regularity in the storm months, and for anyone spending a night in the city rather than on a boat.

We book with Hoi An Express directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers transfers and transport per the itinerary, entrance fees, bottled water and an English-speaking guide, with other languages available at a surcharge.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: The city behind the pier, which most visitors never see
Quang Ninh Museum, a black glass box reflecting the bay
Inside: marine geology and the coal history that built the town
Long Tien Pagoda under Bai Tho Mountain
Works on days the bay cruises are cancelled for weather

fullDescription:
A tandem flight over Ha Long Bay under a powered paraglider, which is the only way to see the whole field of karsts at once.

From a boat you see the towers one at a time as you pass between them. From the air the shape of the bay finally makes sense: roughly 1,600 limestone islands and islets spread across the water, and you can see how the same drowned karst landscape continues under the surface.

Powered paragliding is a paraglider wing with a motor and propeller behind the pilot, so it takes off from flat ground and climbs on its own rather than needing a hill or a tow. You fly tandem, strapped in front of the pilot, which means you do nothing but sit and look.

It is far slower and far quieter than a helicopter, and you are in open air rather than behind glass, which is the whole difference.

Flights are weather-dependent in a way boat trips are not. Wind and low cloud ground them, so if the bay is in one of its grey, still-aired moods the flight will move rather than take off in bad conditions. Build a spare day around it if you can.

A GoPro is included, so the footage is taken care of and you are not holding a phone at altitude.

We book with The Sky Bros directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the tandem flight, air-conditioned transport to and from the field, paragliding gear, the GoPro camera, all fees and taxes, and insurance.

Two hours including transfers and waiting for the right air. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: See all 1,600 karsts at once instead of one at a time
Tandem flight: you sit, the pilot flies
Powered wing, so it launches from flat ground
Open air and quiet, unlike a helicopter
GoPro footage included; flights move if the wind is wrong

fullDescription:
A day ticket on the open-top bus that loops Ha Long city, useful for a very specific situation.

Ha Long's sights are spread out along a long coastal strip rather than clustered in an old quarter. The city runs several kilometres end to end, the two halves are joined by the Bai Chay bridge, and walking between the museum, the pagoda, the markets and the cable car is not realistic in the heat. A loop bus with a day ticket solves that without negotiating a taxi fare each time.

The audio guide runs in eight languages, which on this route matters because Ha Long gets a lot of visitors who are not working in English.

Where this earns its place: if you have a night in Ha Long city either side of a bay cruise, or if a cruise is cancelled for weather, a day ticket turns an empty day into a usable one. It is also the low-effort option with tired legs or small children, since you are never more than a loop away from where you started.

Where it does not: it does not go on the water. Ha Long Bay itself is a boat trip, and the bus is the city, so this is the complement to a cruise rather than a substitute for one.

Frequency is lower than in European cities running the same brand, so check the timetable at the first stop rather than assuming a bus every ten minutes.

We book with City Sightseeing Worldwide directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the one-day hop-on hop-off ticket, stops near the major sights and the eight-language audio guide.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Ha Long city runs for kilometres; the sights are not walkable
One-day ticket, hop off at the museum, pagoda and markets
Audio guide in eight languages
Turns a weather-cancelled cruise day into a usable one
Check the timetable at the first stop; frequency is modest

fullDescription:
Two days, two versions of the same limestone, with everything already paid for before you leave Hanoi.

Ninh Binh is the karst landscape on land. The same towers that rise out of the sea at Ha Long rise here out of rice paddies and a slow river, which is why it gets called the inland bay. Tam Coc is the two-hour boat trip through three river caves, rowed by locals who famously work the oars with their feet. Mua Cave is the climb: several hundred stone steps to a dragon on the ridge, and the view from the top is the one that put Ninh Binh on the map.

Day two moves to Ha Long Bay and the sea version of the same geology.

All-inclusive here means what it says: entrance fees to every listed attraction are covered, which on this route is not trivial. Ninh Binh charges separately at Tam Coc, Mua Cave and Hoa Lu, and a trip quoted without them can add up quickly at the gate.

Pickup and drop-off is in Hanoi's Old Quarter, so this runs as a two-day loop out of Hanoi rather than something you join in Ninh Binh.

The drive from Hanoi to Ninh Binh is around two hours each way on good road, which is why the itinerary starts early.

We book with Hanoi Explore Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers Hanoi Old Quarter pickup and drop-off, entrance fees to all listed attractions, the two-hour Tam Coc boat trip and the Mua Cave climb.

Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: The same karst inland at Ninh Binh and at sea in Ha Long
Tam Coc rowed through three river caves, oars worked by foot
Mua Cave: several hundred steps to the ridge dragon
Entrance fees included, which Ninh Binh charges site by site
Runs as a loop from Hanoi's Old Quarter

fullDescription:
Ha Long Bay in a single day from Hanoi, with a VIP limousine handling the part nobody enjoys.

The drive is the reason this tour is built the way it is. Hanoi to Ha Long is around two and a half hours each way on the expressway, so a day trip is roughly five hours in a vehicle either side of the water. A limousine van, which in Vietnam means eight or nine reclining seats instead of sixteen upright ones, changes what those five hours feel like more than anything on the boat does.

On the water you are among roughly 1,600 limestone islands and islets, a drowned karst landscape that kept going below sea level as the water rose. The towers are the tops of what was once a range of hills.

A day trip sees the central bay. For a first visit, or for anyone short on days in Vietnam, the central bay is the bay: it holds the islands everyone comes to see.

The English-speaking guide is included on the group option. Other languages are available with a surcharge on the private option, which is worth asking about before booking if English is not your first language.

We book with Vn biketour directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the VIP limousine, bottled water and the English-speaking guide on the group option.

Eight hours. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Limousine van: reclining seats for five hours of driving
Roughly 1,600 karst islands, the tops of a drowned range
Covers the central bay, the classic Ha Long day
Other-language guides available on the private option
Runs from Hanoi and back in one day
